That is the silent-pass channel this concern names, surviving in a narrower form.

Verified by loading the pre-fix module (6516d5e9f7c) beside the new one and scanning four mutants of the live retirement push: OLD counted 1 site on each (dead push read as live), NEW counts 0 on each. The clean tree is unaffected — all 10 real sites still scan, all bounded.

Fix: `_COMMENT_WORD_START = " \t;&|()<>"`, bash's whole metacharacter set, documented as a sixth exactness axis with the under-strip/silent failure direction spelled out.

evidence:
ADDRESSED at c61eaf114c2. The finding reproduces exactly, on both halves.

Measured on the real tree: only 2 of 10 live site lines contain a `#` at all (`cron_watch_issue_1739.sh:132`, match [63,72), hash at 76; `cron_watch_issue_2091.sh:52`, match [65,74), hash at 78), and on both the hash falls AFTER the match end. A quote-blind `split("#", 1)[0]` stripper yields an identical site set and identical bound flags across all six wrappers, and `_LIVE` passes identically both ways — so the round-3 rationale ("every watch push line carries a `#` a naive strip would cut into") was false, and the control billed as the over-strip guard controlled nothing.

The code is kept, because a real shape does need it: a `#` inside a quoted argument BEFORE the push variable. `_LIVE_HASH_BEFORE_SITE` builds that from two ADJACENT live lines of `cron_watch_issue_2091.sh` — the `echo "$(ts) #${ISSUE} ..."` log line at 51 and the retirement push at 52 — fused with `&&` onto one physical line, the wrappers' own logging idiom.

Two changes, not one: (1) the stated rationale in `_strip_bash_comment` and in the `_LIVE` block comment is corrected to that shape, and scoped honestly (the trailing-message hash is INERT); (2) `test_quote_tracking_is_load_bearing_when_a_hash_precedes_the_site` RUNS the naive strip rather than asserting about it — quote-aware gives one bounded site, quote-blind gives zero. Verified failing under truncation before it was committed. `test_quote_blind_stripping_is_indistinguishable_on_the_live_line` pins the corrected scope so the false claim cannot return.
